mission.title: Install and Configure MicroK8s
mission.description: MicroK8s is a lightweight, single-package Kubernetes distribution designed for developers and edge computing. It is ideal for local development, CI/CD pipelines, and IoT applications due to its simplicity and minimal resource requirements. Key trade-offs include limited scalability compared to full Kubernetes clusters and reliance on the Snap package manager.

steps.title: Install MicroK8s
steps.description:
This step installs MicroK8s using the Snap package manager, which is the recommended method for installation.

```bash

sudo snap install microk8s --classic

```

> This installs the latest stable version of MicroK8s.

steps.title: Add User to MicroK8s Group
steps.description:
This step allows your user to run MicroK8s commands without needing sudo.

```bash

sudo usermod -a -G microk8s $USER

newgrp microk8s

```

> Replace $USER with your username if needed.
> This command refreshes your group membership.

steps.title: Verify Installation
steps.description:
Check that MicroK8s is running and the Kubernetes nodes are ready.

```bash

microk8s status --wait-ready

microk8s kubectl get nodes

```

> This waits until MicroK8s is fully initialized.
> This verifies that the Kubernetes node is ready.

steps.title: Enable Add-ons
steps.description:
MicroK8s comes with several add-ons that can be enabled for additional functionality.

```bash

microk8s enable dns

microk8s enable dashboard

```

> Enables the DNS add-on for service discovery.
> Enables the Kubernetes dashboard for UI management.

uninstall.title: Uninstall MicroK8s
uninstall.description:
This step removes MicroK8s from your system. Be aware that this will delete all Kubernetes resources and configurations.

```bash

sudo snap remove microk8s

```

> This command will remove MicroK8s and all associated data.

uninstall.title: Remove User from MicroK8s Group
uninstall.description:
This step removes your user from the MicroK8s group to prevent access to MicroK8s commands.

```bash

sudo gpasswd -d $USER microk8s

```

> Replace $USER with your username if needed.

upgrade.title: Upgrade MicroK8s
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you have a backup of your Kubernetes resources. This step upgrades MicroK8s to the latest version.

```bash

microk8s stop

sudo snap refresh microk8s

microk8s start

microk8s kubectl get nodes

```

> Stop MicroK8s before upgrading.
> This command upgrades MicroK8s to the latest version.
> Start MicroK8s after the upgrade.
> Verify that the nodes are ready after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'microk8s is not running'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** MicroK8s may not have started properly or is stopped.

**Fix:**
Run 'microk8s start' to start the MicroK8s service.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubectl: command not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubectl command is not available in your PATH.

**Fix:**
Use 'microk8s kubectl' instead of 'kubectl'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubeconfig file may not be set up correctly.

**Fix:**
Run 'microk8s kubectl config view --raw > $HOME/.kube/config' to set up kubeconfig.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'insufficient memory'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The system does not meet the minimum resource requirements.

**Fix:**
Ensure your system has at least 2 vCPU and 4GB RAM.
